doc.title: Mona Hinton interviewed by Milt Fillius and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995

title: Milt's philosophy of giving from the heart
summary: Mona learned from Milt not to resent people who misuse his generosity.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: That’s right. I’ve been very fortunate. In the beginning when Milton and I first got together, I used to think that he allowed people to take advantage of him, and boy I’m telling you I didn’t like that and I would speak my mind.

But I’ll tell you one day he said to me he said, “I have to tell you something,” he said, “when I do something, I do it from my heart,” and he said, “and I don’t feel that anybody’s taking advantage of me. If I do something and someone wants to take that and misuse it or use it in a negative way,” he said, “I have nothing to do with it. That’s between them and their God. I’ve done what I think is right.” And it took me a long time to understand that but I think I’m a much better person once I started following, thinking along those lines like he did. But it’s true. I mean you do what you think is right, and if someone wants to misuse it, you have nothing to do with it, you’ve done your part.
